title: Fours: Double, Double
goal: I can find 4 times a number by doubling two times.

card.desc: Week 2 starts the facts Bristol does not know yet. She already knows her 2s, so today the 4s become double, double: 4 × 7 is 2 × 7 = 14, then 14 + 14 = 28. She checks with arrays and by skip counting by 4s.

win: Double, double! You are a 4s star!

slides.title: On Your Own: Double, Double
slides.text: You learned the 4s trick in class. Now use it on your own. 🐾

slides.title: Think about your book
slides.text: Read each question. Tell a grown-up your answer.
prompts: How does Amy feel right now in the story? How do you know?
What is one new word you read? What does it mean?

items.q: There are 4 cages. Every cage has 2 birds. How many birds?
items.no: Every cage has 2. Skip count by 2s, one time for each cage.

items.q: Ellie has 10 red beads and 4 green beads. To find how many in all, do you multiply or add? Type multiply or add.
items.why: 10 and 4 are not equal groups, so add: 10 + 4 = 14.
items.no: Is there a clue word? Is 10 the same as 4?

slides.title: Double, double
slides.text: 4 × 6: double 6 is 12. Double 12 is 24.
slides.tip: Find the 2s fact. Then double it.

slides.title: How to do 4 × 9
slides.text: Tap the steps in the right order.
slides.why: Read it, find the 2s fact, double it, then say the whole fact.
slides.hint: Start by reading the fact. Next, find the 2s fact. Then double it.

slides.title: Seed rows
slides.text: Marion plants 4 rows. She puts 8 seeds in each row. Make the groups.
slides.why: 4 groups of 8. Double 8 is 16. Double 16 is 32.
slides.hint: Each row is one group. Groups = how many rows. In each group = seeds in one row.

items.why: Turn it around: 4 × 6. Double 6 is 12. Double 12 is 24.

no: 18 + 9 is not a double. Double 18 is 36.

slides.title: Word problems
slides.text: Equal groups? Multiply. Not equal? Add.

items.q: There are 4 dogs. Each dog has 7 spots. How many spots?
items.why: 4 equal groups of 7. Double 7 is 14. Double 14 is 28.

items.q: Amy has 4 hats. Liz has 3 hats. How many hats in all?
items.why: 4 and 3 are not equal groups. Add: 4 + 3 = 7.
items.no: Is there a clue word? Are the groups the same size?

sets.q: For 4 × 9, Liz says: double 9 is 18. What is next?
no: Adding 4 is not a double. 18 + 4 = 22, not 4 × 9.
18 is only 2 × 9. You need 4 groups. Double again.

sets.q: The vet has 4 shelves. Each shelf has 6 jars. How many jars?
sets.why: 4 equal groups of 6: double 6 is 12, double 12 is 24.

sets.q: Liz washed 4 dogs. Then she washed 9 more dogs. How many dogs did she wash?
sets.why: 4 and 9 are not equal groups. Add: 4 + 9 = 13.
sets.no: Is there a clue word? Are the groups the same size?

sets.why: Double 7 is 14. Double 14 is 28. So 4 × 7 = 28, not 24.

no: 14 + 7 is not a double. Double 14 is 28.

sets.q: Amy's mom has 4 cages. Each cage has 8 mice. How many mice?
sets.why: 4 equal groups of 8: double 8 is 16, double 16 is 32.

sets.q: Ellie has 4 stickers. Marion gives her 7 more. How many stickers does Ellie have now?
sets.why: 4 and 7 are not equal groups. Add: 4 + 7 = 11.
sets.no: Is there a clue word? Are the groups the same size?

sets.q: Mia says 4 × 9 = 18. What did she do?
sets.why: Double 9 is 18. She had to double again: 36.
no: 4 × 9 is not 18. Double 18 to get 4 groups.

sets.why: Turn it around: 4 × 9. Double 9 is 18, double 18 is 36.

sets.q: For 4 × 6, Amy says: double 6 is 12. What is next?
no: 12 is only 2 × 6. You need 4 groups. Double again.

sets.q: There are 4 trays. Every tray has 7 cupcakes. How many cupcakes?
sets.why: 4 equal groups of 7: double 7 is 14, double 14 is 28.

sets.q: Marion has 8 books. Liz has 4 books. How many books in all?
sets.why: 8 and 4 are not equal groups. Add: 8 + 4 = 12.
sets.no: Is there a clue word? Are the groups the same size?

sets.why: Double 6 is 12. Double 12 is 24. So 4 × 6 = 24, not 20.

practice.intro: Three tries on each one. Only your first try counts. For 4s: double, then double again.

questions.why: Turn it around: 4 × 10. Double 10 is 20. Double 20 is 40.
questions.no: 10 × 4 is the same as 4 × 10. Double, double.

no: 10 is 4 + 6. The rows are equal, so multiply.
10 + 5 is not a double. Double 10 is 20.

questions.q: There are 4 kittens. Each kitten has 4 paws. How many paws?
questions.why: 4 groups of 4. Double 4 is 8. Double 8 is 16.

questions.q: Marion has 4 ribbons. Ellie has 10 ribbons. How many ribbons in all?
questions.why: 4 and 10 are not equal groups. Add: 4 + 10 = 14.
questions.no: Is there a clue word? Are the groups the same size?

questions.q: Theo says 4 × 8 = 16. What did he do?
questions.why: Double 8 is 16. He had to double again: 32.

pages.title: Part 1: Double it
pages.directions: Double means add the number to itself.

pages.title: Part 2: Double, double
pages.directions: Find the 2s fact. Then double it.

pages.title: Part 3: Draw an array
pages.directions: Draw dots in rows. Then write the fact.

items.text: 10. There are 4 cages. Each cage has 7 bunnies. How many bunnies?
11. Amy has 4 pens. Liz has 7 pens. How many pens?
12. There are 4 dogs. Each dog gets 9 treats. How many treats?

pages.title: Part 5: Book corner
pages.directions: Write one sentence about Amy and the Missing Puppy. Use a capital letter and a period.

items.text: 13. What is the big problem in the story?

teacher.objective: Bristol learns ×4 as double, double: she finds the 2s fact (which she knows) and doubles it (4 × 7 → 14 → 28). She checks with an array split into two halves and with a number line. She keeps sorting equal groups (multiply) from unequal groups (add).
materials: Zoom with screen share: share the class lesson page (code 9110)
At home (ask Tia the day before): about 40 dried beans or cereal pieces, a sheet of paper, a pencil, a folded paper card to cover rows
Her book, Amy and the Missing Puppy
Lesson 3 packet: printed later in the week (it is on Tuesday's task list)

plan.do: Class slides 1–2. Check her materials on camera. She tells the big problem, what Amy has tried, and predicts with a reason.
Class slide 3. She says equal groups or not before each answer; you type or tap for her.
Class slides 4–5. Two piles of 3 beans on camera = double 3. Doubling warm-up; on double 18 she must say "regroup".
Class slides 6–8. 4 piles of 3: push 2 aside, 6 + 6 = 12. Then 4 rows of 6 on paper, cover 2 rows with the card: 12 and 12. Then 4 × 5 by double, double, which matches her 5s.
Class slides 9–11. Count the jumps on fingers (halfway is 16). Order the steps for 4 × 7. She makes 4 piles of 4 beans and tells you the buttons.
Class slides 12–14. She says both doubles before every answer. Turn-around: 7 × 4 = 4 × 7. Sort: she names the box, you tap.
Class slides 15–16. Equal or not before each answer. Then 4 facts on paper with both doubles, held up to the camera.
Class slide 17. Share the course page: tonight only the after-class lesson (ends with Show What You Know) and 10 minutes of reading. Tomorrow in person: the 6s.

watch: Stopping after one double (4 × 9 = 18). Ask: "How many groups is that? 2 or 4?"
Forgetting to regroup when doubling 16 or 18 (writes 26 or 216). Have her line up tens and ones on paper.
Saying 4 × 8 = 24 because she counted 8, 16, 24 (three jumps). Have her count her jumps out loud on her fingers.
Multiplying any two numbers she sees (4 dogs and 6 dogs = 24). Make her say "each" or find that it is missing.

packet_key.answer: Any complete sentence that names the problem (the puppy is missing), with a capital letter and a period.

teacher.notes: Lesson 4 is tomorrow (in person), so the homework tonight is light: the after-class lesson and reading only. Lesson 3's practice and packet are assigned on Tuesday's task list. Show What You Know is at the end of the after-class lesson; a retake gives her a brand-new set of 8 questions. If she scores under 85, open Tuesday with 5 minutes of bean piles (4 piles, push 2 aside, double) before the ×6 lesson. Do not move on to 6s until she can say the doubles for 4 × 6, 4 × 7 and 4 × 8.

tasks: Monday night: do the After-Class Lesson. Finish with Show What You Know.
Monday night: read your book for 10 minutes.

slides.title: Fours: Double, Double
slides.text: You know your 2s. Today they help you with the 4s. 🐾

notes.do: Share your screen on this class lesson page. Ask her to hold up to the camera: about 40 beans (or cereal pieces), a sheet of paper, a pencil, and a folded paper card for covering rows.
notes.say: Today you learn a trick for the 4s. You already know your 2s, and the 2s will do the hard work.
notes.listen: Quick answers (12, 18). If she hesitates on 2s, slow the doubling part down today.

slides.title: The missing puppy
slides.text: Think about Amy and the Missing Puppy.
prompts: What is the big problem in the story?
What has Amy done so far to fix it?
What do you think will happen next? Why?

notes.do: 5–6 minutes. She answers out loud. Tap the gold button for each strong answer.
notes.ask: What is the big problem? What has Amy done so far to fix it? What do you think will happen next, and why?
notes.listen: A full sentence for each, and a reason with "because" on the prediction.

items.q: There are 5 baskets. Each basket has 3 kittens. How many kittens?
items.why: Each basket has 3, so the groups are equal. 5 × 3 = 15.
items.no: Each basket has 3. Skip count by 3s, one time for each basket.

items.q: An array has 2 rows of 5. Which array has the same number?
Liz has 4 balls. Marion has 5 balls. How many balls in all?
items.why: 4 and 5 are not equal groups, so add: 4 + 5 = 9.
items.no: Is there a clue word? Are the groups the same size?

notes.do: On Zoom she says her answer out loud; you type or tap it on the shared screen. Before each answer she says equal groups or not.
notes.listen: 15, 5 rows of 2, and 9. If she says 20 for the balls, she multiplied without a clue word: ask, "Does every girl have the same number?"

slides.title: What is a double?
slides.text: Double means add a number to itself. It is the same as × 2.

steps.text: Double 12: 12 + 12 = 24. Add the ones, then the tens.

slides.tip: You already know your 2s. Every 2s fact is a double!

notes.do: She makes a pile of 3 beans and another pile of 3 beans on camera: double 3.
notes.say: Doubling is just your 2s. 2 × 7 and double 7 are the same thing.
notes.ask: What is double 12? Say the ones first, then the tens.
notes.listen: "2 plus 2 is 4 ones, 1 plus 1 is 2 tens, 24."

slides.title: Doubling
slides.text: Double means add a number to itself.

items.no: Add the ones: 4 + 4. Then the tens: 1 + 1.

items.why: 18 + 18: 8 + 8 = 16 ones. Regroup 10 ones as 1 ten. 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 tens. So 36.
no: You forgot to regroup. 8 + 8 = 16, so carry 1 ten.
16 ones is 1 ten and 6 ones. Carry the ten. Don't write 16.

notes.do: On Zoom she says her answer out loud; you type or tap it on the shared screen. On double 18 she writes 18 + 18 on her paper, tens over tens, and holds it up.
notes.ask: On double 18: what do we do with 16 ones?
notes.listen: "Regroup: 1 ten and 6 ones." 26 or 216 means she did not regroup.

slides.title: 4 groups = 2 groups + 2 groups
slides.text: 4 × 3 means 4 groups of 3.

steps.text: Split the 4 groups into 2 groups and 2 more groups.

slides.tip: 4 is 2 and 2. So ×4 is double, then double again.

notes.do: She makes 4 piles of 3 beans on camera. Then she pushes 2 piles to one side.
notes.say: 4 groups is 2 groups and 2 more groups. The 2 groups are a 2s fact. The other side is the same, so we double it.
notes.ask: How many beans in the 2 piles on the left? On the right? All together?
notes.listen: "6 and 6, so 12." Then she says the fact: 4 × 3 = 12.

slides.title: Double, double: 4 × 6
slides.text: Let's find 4 × 6.
slides.tip: Say it out loud: double 6 is 12, double 12 is 24.

notes.do: She makes 4 rows of 6 beans on her paper and covers the bottom 2 rows with the folded card.
notes.say: The top half is 2 × 6. The bottom half is the same. So double it.
notes.ask: How many in the top 2 rows? Now lift the card. How many in all?

slides.title: Try 4 × 5
slides.text: Use double, double for 4 × 5.

items.why: Double 10 is 20. That is all 4 groups.
Double, double: 5, 10, 20. And your 5s say 4 × 5 = 20 too!
items.no: What did you get after the second double?

notes.do: On Zoom she says her answer out loud; you type or tap it on the shared screen.
notes.say: You already know 4 × 5 from your 5s. Look: the trick gives the same answer. That is how we know it works.
notes.listen: 10, 20, 20. If she says 10 for 4 × 5, she stopped after one double.

slides.title: Check it on a number line
slides.text: 4 × 8 is 4 jumps of 8.

steps.text: After 2 jumps you are at 16. That is 2 × 8.

slides.tip: You can also count by 4s: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32. That is 8 jumps of 4. Same answer!

notes.do: Click through the steps slowly. She counts the jumps on her fingers.
notes.ask: Where are we after 2 jumps? What do the other 2 jumps add?
notes.listen: "16 after 2 jumps, 16 more is 32." If she says 24, she counted 3 jumps: count them together on fingers.

slides.title: How to do 4 × 7
slides.text: Tap the steps in the right order.
slides.why: Read it, find the 2s fact, double it, then say the whole fact.
slides.hint: Start by reading the fact. Next, find the 2s fact. Then double it.

notes.do: On Zoom she says her answer out loud; you type or tap it on the shared screen. She tells you which step comes next; you tap it.
notes.listen: "Because 4 is 2 and 2. Find the 2s, then double."

slides.title: Dog bowls at the vet
slides.text: Amy's mom fills 4 bowls. She puts 4 treats in each bowl. Make the groups.
slides.why: 4 groups of 4. Double 4 is 8. Double 8 is 16. 4 × 4 = 16.
slides.hint: Each bowl is one group. Groups = how many bowls. In each group = treats in one bowl.

notes.do: She makes 4 piles of 4 beans at home and tells you "4 groups, 4 in each"; you click the buttons and Check.

items.why: Start at 8. Double it: 16. Double again: 32.
no: 16 + 8 is not a double. 16 doubled is 32.
Start with the 8, not the 4. 4, 8, 16 is doubling 4.

notes.do: On Zoom she says her answer out loud; you type or tap it on the shared screen. Before every answer she says the two doubles out loud ("9, 18, 36").

slides.title: Turn it around
slides.text: 7 × 4 is the same as 4 × 7. So use double, double!
slides.tip: See a 4 on either side? Think double, double.

notes.say: Remember turn-around facts from last week? The 4 can be first or second.

slides.title: Same answer, same box
slides.text: Tap a card. Then tap the box with its answer.

items.why: Turn it around: 4 × 7. Double 7 is 14, double 14 is 28.

slides.done: Double, double gives the 4s fact every time.

notes.do: On Zoom she says her answer out loud; you type or tap it on the shared screen. She picks a card, says its answer, and tells you which box.
notes.ask: Which card shares the box with 4 × 6? Why?
notes.listen: "Double 12," because 4 × 6 is double 12. She should see that 4 × 8 and double 16 are the same.

slides.title: Word problems
slides.text: Equal groups? Multiply. Not equal? Add.

items.q: Marion has 4 bags. Each bag has 8 dog bones. How many bones?
items.why: 4 equal groups of 8. Double 8 is 16, double 16 is 32.

items.q: Ellie fed 4 big dogs and 6 small dogs. How many dogs did she feed?
no: There are not 4 groups of 6. There is one group of 4 and one group of 6.
2 is 6 − 4. No dogs went away. Put the two groups together.

notes.do: On Zoom she says her answer out loud; you type or tap it on the shared screen. She reads each one aloud and says equal or not before answering.
notes.listen: 32 and 10. 24 for the dogs means she multiplied 4 and 6 without a clue word.

slides.title: Show me on paper
slides.text: Write each fact on your paper. Show both doubles. Hold it up!

steps.text: Get your paper and pencil. Listen for the first fact.

slides.tip: Write three numbers: the number, double it, double again.

notes.do: Say one fact at a time. She writes the three numbers, holds the paper up to the camera, then you click to show the answer.
notes.listen: Three numbers each time. Watch for 4 × 9 written as 9, 18, 27 (adding 9, not doubling). 4 × 10 should be quick: 10, 20, 40.

slides.title: Double, double!
slides.text: 4s = double, then double again.
slides.tip: Tonight: do the after-class lesson and read for 10 minutes. That's all!

notes.do: Share the course page. Show the Lesson 3 task list: only two things tonight.
notes.say: Tomorrow we meet in person and learn the 6s. They use your 5s. Your practice and packet for today come on Tuesday's list.
